# Strategic Plan: logpulse (nginx access-log analyzer CLI)

> Planning document generated by `/blueprint --full`. Cross-references:
> [PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md](PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md), [PRD.md](PRD.md),
> [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), [CLAUDE_CODE_GUIDE.md](CLAUDE_CODE_GUIDE.md).

## 1. Idea description

`logpulse` is a local, single-process Python 3.11 command-line tool for DevOps/SRE
engineers. It streams an nginx access log (file or stdin) and reports four things:

1. Top-10 client IPs by request volume.
2. Top-10 URLs ranked by 4xx/5xx error responses.
3. Hourly request distribution (as a percentage of valid requests).
4. Share of unique User-Agents.

Default output is colored terminal text (Rich). `--json` and `--csv` make it
pipeline-friendly. It processes 1 GB in under 30 seconds on a laptop, stateless,
with no server, database, or cloud dependency.

## 2. Target audience

| Persona | Role | Pain | How we solve it |
|---------|------|------|-----------------|
| Priya, on-call SRE | Reliability engineer | During an incident she needs the top offending IPs and failing URLs from a raw log *now*, without shipping data to a stack | One command, streams the log, prints top IPs/URLs in seconds |
| Marco, DevOps generalist | Platform engineer | `grep/awk` one-liners are error-prone and hard to reuse across teammates | Reproducible CLI with stable JSON/CSV contracts |
| Lena, infra lead | Team lead | Standing up GoAccess/ELK for a one-off triage is overkill and off-budget | Zero-infra, pip-installable, $0 tool |

## 3. Competitive analysis

| Competitor | What it does | Weaknesses | Our difference |
|-----------|--------------|------------|----------------|
| GoAccess | Real-time terminal/HTML log dashboard | C build/deps, broad feature set, config to learn for a quick answer | Narrow, opinionated 4-metric report; pure pip; scriptable JSON/CSV |
| Logstash + Elastic + Kibana | Full ingestion/search/visualization stack | Heavy infra, RAM-hungry, cost, ops burden | No server, no index, no cost; runs in one process |
| AWStats | Perl log analytics with historical reports | CGI/Perl era UX, stateful DB of history, HTML-first | Stateless streaming, terminal-first, modern CLI |
| grep / awk | Ad-hoc one-liners | Not reusable, no structured output, easy to get wrong | Tested parser, stable exit codes, JSON/CSV for pipelines |

## 4. Unique selling proposition

The fastest way to get the four questions that matter during triage answered from a
raw nginx log — one pip install, one command, no infrastructure, structured output
you can pipe.

## 5. Business model

Open source, $0 budget, no monetization. Value is developer time saved and
zero-infra triage. Distribution: PyPI + GitHub. No paid tier, no telemetry.

## 6. Technology stack

| Component | Technology | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-----|
| Language | Python 3.11 | Ubiquitous on SRE laptops; strong stdlib; dataclasses/typing |
| CLI framework | Click | Declarative options, standard exit-code handling, help/UX |
| Terminal rendering | Rich | Color tables/bars without hand-rolling ANSI |
| Data modeling | dataclasses | Typed, zero-dependency result structures |
| Packaging | pip / pyproject.toml | `pip install logpulse`, console entry point |
| Tests | pytest | Standard, fast, fixtures for sample logs |

## 7. Timeline (one weekend)

| Day | Stage | Result |

| Sat AM | Parser + streaming core | Lines parsed into records, stdin/file input |

## 9. Risks

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Non-standard log formats break the parser | High | Medium | Configurable format; count and report skipped lines; never crash on a bad line |
| Unique-UA tracking blows up memory on huge cardinality | Medium | High | Bounded cardinality set with `--max-unique` cap; exit code `4` on exhaustion instead of OOM |
| 30 s/1 GB target missed | Medium | Medium | Streaming, compiled-regex fast path, no per-line allocations beyond need; benchmark in CI |
| Scope creep (dashboards, geo-IP, real-time) | Medium | Medium | MoSCoW `Won't` list is explicit; keep the 4-metric focus |

## 10. Budget

| Item | Monthly | Comment |
|------|---------|---------|
| Infrastructure | $0 | Runs locally, no servers |
| Dependencies | $0 | All open source (Click, Rich, pytest) |
| Distribution | $0 | PyPI + GitHub are free |
| **Total** | **$0** | Matches the $0 constraint |

## 11. Feature Roadmap (prioritization)

### MoSCoW

| Feature | MoSCoW | Rationale |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| Streaming line parser (combined format) | **Must** | Nothing works without parsed records |
| Top-10 IPs | **Must** | Core triage question #1 |
| Top-10 URLs by 4xx/5xx | **Must** | Core triage question #2 |
| Hourly request distribution (%) | **Must** | Core triage question #3 |
| Unique User-Agent share | **Must** | Core triage question #4 |
| Colored terminal output (Rich) | **Must** | Default UX for the operator |
| `--json` output | **Must** | Pipeline/automation contract |
| `--csv` output | **Should** | Spreadsheet/pipeline convenience |
| Read from stdin (`-`) | **Should** | `tail -f`-less piping, `zcat` composition |
| Configurable log format | **Should** | Non-default nginx formats |
| `--top N` override | **Could** | Flexibility beyond 10 |
| Gzip auto-detection | **Could** | Convenience; can pipe `zcat` instead |
| Real-time follow / dashboard | **Won't** | Out of scope; that is GoAccess territory |
| GeoIP / reverse DNS enrichment | **Won't** | Adds data deps and latency; not in MVP |
| Database / history persistence | **Won't** | Violates stateless-streaming constraint |

### RICE scoring (Must + Should)

| Feature | Reach (1-10) | Impact (1-5) | Confidence (%) | Effort (days) | RICE Score |
|---------|--------------|--------------|----------------|---------------|------------|
| Streaming line parser | 10 | 5 | 100 | 0.5 | 100.0 |
| Top-10 IPs | 10 | 5 | 100 | 0.25 | 200.0 |
| Top-10 URLs by 4xx/5xx | 10 | 5 | 100 | 0.25 | 200.0 |
| Hourly distribution (%) | 9 | 4 | 100 | 0.25 | 144.0 |
| Unique User-Agent share | 8 | 4 | 90 | 0.5 | 57.6 |
| Colored terminal output | 10 | 3 | 100 | 0.5 | 60.0 |
| `--json` output | 8 | 4 | 100 | 0.25 | 128.0 |
| `--csv` output | 6 | 3 | 90 | 0.25 | 64.8 |
| Read from stdin | 7 | 3 | 90 | 0.25 | 75.6 |
| Configurable log format | 5 | 3 | 70 | 0.5 | 21.0 |

Implementation order follows RICE descending, subject to the dependency that the
parser must land before any aggregator. See [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).

## Definition of Done

A feature is "Done" when:
- [ ] Code written and imports/builds without errors
- [ ] Unit tests pass (coverage >= 80% on parser + aggregators)
- [ ] Integration test passes (end-to-end `analyze` on a sample log)
- [ ] Code review passed (`/review` score >= 8/10)
- [ ] Documentation updated (README, guide)
- [ ] No known Critical/High issues (`/security-audit` on parsing/IO paths)
- [ ] Performance check: 1 GB synthetic log processed in < 30 s on the dev laptop
